title: Surya Roshni Ltd - 500336 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue ₹2,163 crore (+1% YoY) and EBITDA ₹170 crore, down from ₹211 crore; management guides FY27 EBITDA ₹680–700 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was flat YoY at ₹2,163 crore, while EBITDA fell to ₹170 crore (7.9% margin) from ₹211 crore and PAT to ₹98 crore from ₹130 crore. Steel Pipe and Strip volume hit a record 2.6 lakh tons, but EBITDA per ton fell to ₹5,121 from ₹6,708 as exports went to nearly nil after the Middle East crisis. Lighting revenue grew 9% YoY to ₹501 crore but EBITDA dipped to ₹44 crore. Management guided FY27 volume of 11 lakh tons and combined EBITDA of ₹680–700 crore, which analysts questioned against the implied per-ton economics; the company remains debt-free with ₹337 crore net cash.

segments.name: Steel Pipe & Strip
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue ₹1,662 crore and EBITDA ₹126 crore on record 2.6 lakh tons; FY26 volume 9.04 lakh tons, 43% value-added, utilisation 78–80%. Exports were 1.36 lakh tons in FY26 and dropped to nearly nil in Q4 due to the Middle East crisis.

segments.name: Lighting & Consumer Durables
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue ₹501 crore (+9% YoY) with PBT ₹33 crore vs ₹37 crore; March 2026 was the highest monthly sales month in every category. Professional Lighting FY26 revenue ₹473 crore (26% share) with order book ₹160 crore; Wire & Cable FY26 revenue ₹38 crore, FY27 target ₹260 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 combined EBITDA guided at ₹680–700 crore (Steel ₹470–480 crore, Lighting ~₹200 crore); management said it could reach ₹750 crore before a ~₹40–50 crore labour-code impact.
FY27 steel volume target 11 lakh tons (+21–22%); Q1 FY27 volume guided at ~2.65 lakh tons with Steel EBITDA of ₹120–125 crore.
FY27 steel revenue ~₹7,200 crore and group revenue ₹9,400–9,500 crore (+24–25%) per management.
Exports targeted above 2.5 lakh tons in FY27 (vs 1.36 lakh tons), with US order book ~65,000 tons and ~10,000 tons/month added from June; export EBITDA cited at ₹9,000–10,000 per ton.
Steel EBITDA per ton assumed at ~₹4,700 for FY27; Lighting value growth target 22–25% annually over the medium term.
Wire & Cable FY27 revenue target ₹260 crore, on track for ₹500–600 crore in three years.
capex_capacity: Capacity rose ~2 lakh tons over the last 1.5 years; capacity is about 1.4 million tons now and expected to reach ~1.6 million tons in FY27.
A further ~3 lakh tons is planned, taking capacity to ~1.9 million tons in FY28–FY29 (per management).
Seamless-to-ERW/ONGC-linked capex needs 9–10 months; volume impact expected in FY28 and excluded from the 11 lakh ton target.
Capex policy stated as one-third of profit to capex, one-third to working capital and growth, one-third to shareholders.
demand_pricing: Steel order book about ₹1,000 crore-plus, led by exports, spiral and some domestic API orders; H1 FY27 expected to be the highest-ever half for value-added sales.
North America export order book ~65,000 tons; management expects ~1.2 lakh tons of US exports in FY27.
Government/API/tender business is about 15–16% of volume; water pipes plus spiral take it to about 28–30%.
API and spiral EBITDA per ton fell from about ₹12,000 (FY23) to ₹5,600 (FY26) per an analyst's figures, which management acknowledged; tendering competition has risen.
Imported raw material is about 30–35% of input cost; higher input and fuel costs and the labour code (₹30–50 crore impact) pressure FY27 margins.
Steel HR coil availability was tight for 3–4 months due to gas shortages linked to the Middle East crisis; management says it is now largely resolved.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 miss expectations when competitors grew strongly, and will the 12,000 tons of missed exports be recovered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed the Middle East crisis, which cut exports to near nil and left about 12,000 tons of ready material unshipped, plus a domestic steel shortage. It said Q1 FY27 volume will be a record ~2.65 lakh tons.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 EBITDA of ₹680–700 crore credible given the implied ₹4,700 per ton?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the guidance already includes risks such as input cost inflation, fuel and power costs, and labour-code costs of ₹30–40 crore; it could reach ₹750 crore. It cited export EBITDA of ₹9,000–10,000 per ton offsetting pressure in oil and gas and domestic businesses.

qa_highlights.question: Why is volume growth only ~70,000–80,000 tons domestically if exports add 1.1–1.25 lakh tons?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said government spending on oil and gas and water schemes is assumed to stay low, so it kept targets conservative; it said 11 lakh tons is a minimum and could be exceeded.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Lighting demerger and buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the demerger will be discussed with the board once the crisis ends, possibly by the next board meeting. It said a buyback is being reconsidered now that the regulations have been reintroduced, with no timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Why has steel growth lagged the industry over 4–5 years and why has API/spiral EBITDA per ton fallen?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed slow growth to no major capex during COVID and two years after, and a focus on higher-margin products. It said API/spiral per-ton EBITDA halved as tendering is uncontrolled and competition has increased.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk of steel availability constraints for Q1–Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the HR coil shortage lasted 3–4 months due to a demand surge and gas shortages, is now largely sorted, and that domestic HR coil supply is growing each year.

risks_watch: Execution on the 2.65 lakh ton Q1 FY27 volume and recovery of the ~12,000 tons of missed exports.
Whether steel EBITDA per ton recovers from ₹5,121 (Q4) toward the ~₹4,700 FY27 assumption and the export mix ramps (US ~1.2 lakh tons).
Middle East crisis effects on exports, gas availability and HR coil supply.
Input cost pressure (imported raw material 30–35% of cost), labour-code costs and government spending delays on water and oil & gas projects.
Credibility of guidance: management has missed volume targets in consecutive quarters, as an analyst pointed out.
Lighting demerger timing and the buyback decision, both not yet confirmed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY27 and the US export opportunity, but defensive when questioned on repeated missed targets and falling per-ton margins. Management attributed the shortfall to external shocks and repeatedly reassured investors with few hard assumptions.
key_quotes: I can assure you that for FY27, whatever the situation with the Middle East crisis, considering all that, it will be the best year in history for Surya Roshni.
Our Q1 will have the highest-ever volume, around 2.65 lakh tons in Q1 itself and we will grow by about 27% to 28%.
I often say our relationship with the bank has ended; now our relationship is only with the shareholders.
Look, two things. One, as far as risk is concerned, the numbers we have just told you are telling these numbers after considering all these risk factors.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 volume +21-22% to 11 lakh tons and group revenue of ₹9,400-9,500 crore (+24-25%), backed by a ~₹1,000 crore+ steel order book, ~65,000 t US export order book and capacity rising from 1.4 to 1.6 mt in FY27, but EBITDA guidance of ₹680-700 crore implies pressure from falling per-ton economics (~₹4,700/t vs ₹4,553 FY26) and labour-code costs.
